references.text: The creation account where God separates light from darkness: [ref:Gen 1:3-4|Genesis 1:3-4]. The light shines in the darkness from the very beginning of creation, and the darkness has not overcome it.
Job speaks of God's light shining in the darkness: [ref:Job 29:3|Job 29:3]. God's light guides through the darkness.
[ref:Ps 18:29|Psalm 18:29] – The Lord makes my darkness bright; he is the one who lights up my darkness. An image of God's light overcoming darkness.
[ref:Ps 119:105|Psalm 119:105] – God's word is a lamp for my feet and a light for my path. The Word (Logos) as light in the darkness is a recurring biblical theme.

Isaiah's prophecy that the people walking in darkness will see a great light: [ref:Isa 9:2|Isaiah 9:2]. The light shines in the darkness and brings hope to those living in the land of the shadow of death.
[ref:Isa 60:1-2|Isaiah 60:1-2] – The Lord's light shines upon his people, even though darkness covers the earth. Darkness cannot overpower God's light.
[ref:John 1:9|John 1:9] expands on this verse by explaining that the true light, which gives light to everyone, was coming into the world.
[ref:John 3:19-20|John 3:19-20] – The light has come into the world, but people loved darkness more than light. Darkness tries to reject the light, but cannot overcome it.

Jesus declares himself to be the light of the world in [ref:John 8:12|John 8:12]: "Whoever follows me will never walk in darkness, but will have the light of life." This expands on the meaning of the light shining in the darkness.

[ref:John 12:35-36|John 12:35-36] – Jesus urges his disciples to believe in the light while they still have it, so that darkness will not overtake them. The same theme of light and darkness as in 1:5.
[ref:Rom 1:21|Romans 1:21] – People became darkened in their thinking and did not understand God's revelation. A parallel to the idea that darkness did not grasp (understand/overcome) the light.
[ref:Eph 5:8-9|Ephesians 5:8-9] – Paul contrasts darkness and light and urges believers to walk as children of light. The light overcomes the deeds of darkness.
[ref:1 John 1:5-6|1 John 1:5-6] – "God is light, and in him there is no darkness at all." John expands on this same theme of the contrast between light and darkness.

[ref:1 John 2:8-9|1 John 2:8-9] – The darkness is passing away, and the true light is already shining. The light is about to overcome darkness, in line with the idea that darkness did not overcome the light.
